provenance.assigned_by: multimodal reasoning over class definitions + measured per-class segment statistics
provenance.roughness_family: 2D shallow-water land-cover tables (HEC-RAS 2D / FEMA), rooted in Chow (1959) Table 5-6
provenance.roughness_family_rejected: Engman (1986) overland-flow coefficients — calibrated for millimetre-deep sheet flow, 10-20x larger, not defensible at 5 m resolution and ~0.1 m depth
provenance.baseline_anchor: grass_turf is pinned to the solver's existing scalar MANNING_N = 0.040 so the experiment isolates redistribution from recalibration

soil_parameters_are_now_a_measured_compa.why: Track A's first pass declined to supply Ks and soil Smax on the grounds that SSURGO measures them. That was a judgement call, and it has been replaced by an experiment: both parameterisations are built and both are run against the Gee Creek gauge. See run_site3_ian_segmented.py --arms vision_soil.
soil_parameters_are_now_a_measured_compa.vision_route: vision_ks_mm_hr_dry / vision_soil_storage_m below, from the class map
soil_parameters_are_now_a_measured_compa.why_it_matters_beyond_this_site: SSURGO exists only in the United States. If the premise is 'any coordinate -> a twin', the size of the gap between a soil survey and a vision estimate is what decides whether the pipeline is US-only or global.
soil_parameters_are_now_a_measured_compa.fairness: The same AMC-III wet-antecedent factor the solver already applies to SSURGO Ksat is applied to the vision Ks. Both sides are dry-condition saturated conductivities, so correcting only one would compare a wet soil against a dry one and the vision arm would infiltrate ~14x too much.

references: USACE HEC-RAS 2D Modeling User's Manual — land-cover Manning's n tables.
Engman, E.T. (1986) Roughness coefficients for routing surface runoff, JIDE 112(1) — the rejected family, cited so the choice is auditable.
Zinke, P.J. (1967) Forest interception studies in the United States — canopy interception 1-2 mm.

water.n_basis: Chow 1959 — clean, straight natural channel / open water surface, 0.030-0.040.
water.storage_basis: A free water surface has no storage to fill; rain joins it directly.
water.impervious_basis: Rain on open water becomes surface water immediately; it does not infiltrate here.
water.vision_ks_basis: No infiltration through a free water surface.

building_roof.n_basis: Smooth manufactured surface. Matches the 0.015 both mesh solvers already use for roofs, so this class does not move a value the project had already set deliberately.
building_roof.storage_basis: 0.5 mm depression storage on a pitched roof — shallow, since a roof is built to shed.

road_paved.n_basis: Chow 1959 — smooth asphalt, 0.013. The smoothest surface in the domain.
road_paved.storage_basis: 1 mm; crowned and drained, but with real texture depth and gutter ponding.
road_paved.impervious_basis: By definition; already how the solver's OSM mask treats these cells.

impervious_other.material: concrete / compacted gravel — driveways, parking, sidewalks, pool decks
impervious_other.n_basis: Slightly rougher than a highway-grade road: broom-finished concrete, joints, and gravel aprons. Chow's concrete range 0.012-0.018.
impervious_other.storage_basis: 1.5 mm; flatter and less deliberately drained than a road.
impervious_other.impervious_basis: 0.90 rather than 1.00 — this class is inferred spectrally, not from a mapped footprint, so a fraction of it is genuinely compacted bare ground rather than sealed surface.
impervious_other.vision_ks_basis: 90 % sealed; the pervious remainder is compacted gravel/verge.

tree_canopy.material: forest floor beneath closed canopy — litter over sandy soil
tree_canopy.n_basis: HEC-RAS 2D / FEMA land-cover tables for forest, 0.10-0.12; Chow's 'heavy stand of timber, little undergrowth, flood stage below branches' is 0.10. Trunks, roots, litter and understory obstruct flow. 3x the scalar this class currently gets.
tree_canopy.storage_basis: 1.5 mm canopy interception for a closed broadleaf/mixed stand, plus ~3 mm litter storage.
tree_canopy.impervious_basis: Fully pervious; SSURGO supplies the soil beneath.
tree_canopy.vision_ks_basis: Rawls et al. (1982) sand, 210 mm/hr. Florida flatwoods forest floor is fine sand, and root macropores and litter keep it open — the highest-conductivity surface in the domain.
tree_canopy.vision_soil_storage_basis: Rooting depth ~1.5 m x 0.25 drainable porosity. Trees root deepest and so command the largest profile.

shrub_scrub.n_basis: FEMA land-cover tables, shrub/scrub 0.05-0.07. Denser near the ground than forest but without the litter mat.
shrub_scrub.storage_basis: 2 mm; less leaf area than closed canopy, little litter.
shrub_scrub.vision_ks_basis: Slightly below forest: sandy, but less macropore development under palmetto scrub.

grass_turf.material: managed turf / pasture over sandy soil
grass_turf.n_basis: FEMA grassland/pasture 0.035-0.05. Deliberately set to 0.040 — the exact scalar the solver uses domain-wide today — so that any change in the gauge metrics is attributable to the classes that MOVED, not to a quiet shift in the baseline.
grass_turf.vision_ks_basis: Rawls loamy sand, 61 mm/hr. Managed turf is mown, trafficked and partly compacted, so well below the forest floor on the same parent sand.
grass_turf.vision_soil_storage_basis: ~0.5 m rooting depth x 0.25. Turf roots shallowly.

bare_soil.n_basis: Chow 1959, bare earth 0.020-0.025. Smoother than turf, rougher than pavement.
bare_soil.vision_ks_basis: Between loamy sand and sandy loam: exposed sand crusts and compacts without a root mat.
bare_soil.vision_soil_storage_basis: ~0.5 m x 0.25; no deep root system to open the profile.

wetland_marsh.material: emergent herbaceous wetland / cypress dome margin
wetland_marsh.n_basis: FEMA emergent-wetland 0.05-0.08. Dense standing stems through the flow depth make this the second-roughest class here.
wetland_marsh.storage_basis: Zero. A wetland sits at the water table and has no unfilled surface store — the same reasoning that gives SSURGO's depressional soils zero soil storage.
wetland_marsh.impervious_basis: Pervious in principle, but saturated in practice; the SSURGO storage cap already forces these cells to shed.
wetland_marsh.vision_ks_basis: Organic, saturated, and sitting at the water table — effectively no capacity.
wetland_marsh.vision_soil_storage_basis: Zero — a wetland sits at the water table, the same reasoning SSURGO applies to its depressional soils.
